title: finding(app-shell): a dataset filter built with After on a date column reads back as an operator that column does not offer
body:
Found by the `os-dev` seat implementing objectui#9372, in the file that card repairs. ⛔ Deliberately not fixed there: it is a different defect on the READ half, and repairing it is a choice between two shapes that wants its own reading.

## The defect

`conditionToGroup` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/datasetFilterCondition.ts`) reads a stored `$gt` back as the builder operator `greaterThan`. But this bridge also WRITES `$gt` for `after` — `OP_TO_MONGO` maps `greaterThan` and `after` onto the same token, and `MONGO_TO_OP` can only pick one of them coming back.

`after` is the entry a **date** field offers. `greaterThan` is not in the date bucket at all. So a dataset filter an author built with **After** on a date column reads back, on reopen, as an operator that column's dropdown does not list.

`before` / `$lt` / `lessThan` is the same pair, one line down.

## Measured

Run against `packages/app-shell/dist` and `packages/components/dist` built from `5c82df068`:

```
read-back operator for a stored $gt: greaterThan | representable: true
date bucket offers: equals notEquals isEmpty isNotEmpty before after between isNull isNotNull
=> date bucket contains the read-back operator? false
control — number bucket contains it? true
```

The control matters: `greaterThan` IS a real member of the number bucket, so the `false` above is a reading about the date bucket specifically, not a lookup that answers `false` for everything.

## The consequence, NOT measured here

`filter-builder.tsx`'s own docblock states what happens to an operator the dropdown no longer lists — objectui#4768, verbatim: *"the operator buckets are per field type and do not nest, so that update could leave `in` on a text column — an operator the dropdown no longer lists, which rendered as a BLANK trigger."* That is the same condition reached by a different route, so the expected consequence is a blank operator trigger on reopen.

⚠️ I did not drive that render, so treat it as the documented behaviour of the component rather than as a measurement of this route. Whoever takes this should confirm it first — it decides whether this is cosmetic drift or a control the author cannot read.

## Why it is not objectui#9372's to fix

objectui#9372 rules on the WRITE half: an operator this bridge cannot express must leave the stored filter alone rather than erase it. This is the read half, it loses no data, and the repair is a genuine choice:

- **A.** Give `after` / `before` their own tokens so the round trip is exact. ⛔ Blocked on the vocabulary question — see below.
- **B.** Make `MONGO_TO_OP` field-type-aware, so a `$gt` on a date column reads back as `after`. Keeps one token, moves the ambiguity to where the type is known. Costs `conditionToGroup` a `fields` argument it does not take today.
- **C.** Rule that the collapse is correct and add `greaterThan` / `lessThan` to the date bucket. Changes what the dropdown offers on dates, which is `@object-ui/components`' call rather than this inspector's.

## Related

- objectui#9306 — the open decision on filter-builder's two operator vocabularies. It already names `before`/`after` folding onto `less_than`/`greater_than` as an unsettled membership question and says whoever rules must restate that membership explicitly. ⇒ **this card is the concrete, reachable-today instance of that question**; direction A above is not takeable before it is ruled. Not a duplicate: objectui#9306 asks which vocabulary is canonical, this one records a round trip that is lossy in app-shell regardless of the answer.
- objectui#9372 / objectui#9363 — the write-half repairs in the same file. Both leave this untouched.
- The refusal of exactly this shape is already written down in that file's neighbourhood: `$exists` was refused as a spelling of `is_not_null` partly because *"the round trip is lossy … silently rewriting the author's choice on reopen"*. The `after` / `$gt` pair is that same lossy round trip, already shipped.

Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's; no labels or assignee set by the finder.

Filed by the `os-dev` seat for objectui#9372 through the repo-scoped REST issues endpoint (MCP was rate-limited this session), from session `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`.
